Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberForge Security Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberForge Security's results for the second quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Security Officer; and Rachel Kim, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. CyberForge Security continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in Q2, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about Nexus 4.0 and the resulting acceleration in multi-year deals is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities. First, accelerating our annual recurring revenue growth, where we hit total ARR of $528 million, up 14.8% quarter-over-quarter from $460 million and 42.3% year-over-year from $371 million, marking our 11th straight quarter of acceleration thanks to net new ARR of $68 million, a dollar-based net expansion rate of 118%, and net retention of 112%, fueled by macro tailwinds like rising cybersecurity budgets post major breaches and innovations such as our GenAI Zero-Trust Orchestrator. Second, outperforming on billings against guidance, delivering $452 million that beat the high end of our $440 million to $450 million range by 0.4% at the midpoint, with 26% year-over-year growth and 15% quarter-over-quarter, led by enterprise deals over $1 million ACV surging 35% and balanced regional strength. Third, ramping R&D investment to 29.7% of revenue at $178 million on $600 million quarterly revenue, expanding from last year to outpace peers and power AI/ML threat intelligence, zero-trust SASE evolution, endpoint protection, and emerging tech like homomorphic encryption. Fourth, boosting competitive win rates to 68% overall, up 450 basis points sequentially and 1,000 basis points year-over-year, dominating in EDR/XDR at 74%, SASE/ZTNA at 65%, and gaining regionally from North America to APAC through product velocity and partner ecosystems. Fifth, driving platform adoption to 78% of total ACV versus point products dropping below 15%, as customers consolidate to avoid alert fatigue and high TCO, with our SecureNet One-like architecture delivering unified intelligence and 128% NRR. And sixth, providing clear next-quarter billings guidance of $272 million to $282 million, implying 10-14% sequential and 25-28% year-over-year growth toward our full-year $1.15 billion to $1.18 billion target, supported by segment strength in network, cloud, and endpoint security.

These priorities position us to capture share in a consolidating market amid escalating threats.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for Q2 was $600 million, representing a 42% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 90% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 80%, while operating expenses were $450 million. Net income was $100 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.85. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

Let me expand on our ARR performance, which remains our north star metric, capturing the annualized value of our subscription contracts across platforms like ForgeShield Endpoint, QuantumGuard Cloud Native Protection, and our AI-powered Nexus Threat Intelligence suite. Total ARR ended the quarter at $528 million, up 14.8% QoQ from $460 million and a robust 42.3% YoY from $371 million in Q2 2023. Net new ARR added was $68 million, with DBNER at 118%—over 70% from upsells and cross-sells—and NRR improving to 112%, driven by 3x adoption growth in advanced modules like GenAI Zero-Trust Orchestrator for AI workload protection.

Key drivers include macro tailwinds in cybersecurity spending, with Gartner forecasting $215 billion globally in 2024, up 15% YoY, as enterprises prioritize security after incidents like the Change Healthcare ransomware and nation-state threats to critical infrastructure. Technical innovation shone through with Nexus 4.0, our ML-driven autonomous EDR platform, closing 25 deals over $1 million ARR, including a $15 million multi-year contract with a top-5 global bank for hybrid cloud segmentation. Hyperscaler integrations with AWS Bedrock, Azure Sentinel, and Google Chronicle ramped cloud security ARR 25% QoQ to 35% of total.

Regionally: Americas at 72% of ARR grew 16.2% QoQ and 48% YoY, boosted by FedRAMP High for U.S. federal wins; EMEA at 18% rose 12.5% QoQ and 38% YoY on NIS2 compliance and a €20 million ARR expansion with a DAX 40 insurer; APAC at 10% increased 11.8% QoQ and 28% YoY via telco partnerships like Singtel and NTT amid PDPA pushes.

Our $2.5 billion ThreatLynx acquisition is accretive, adding $120 million ARR run-rate from deception tech. We guide Q3 QoQ ARR growth of 13-15% and full-year FY24 ARR of $2.25-2.3 billion, implying 45%+ YoY.

On billings, we reported $452 million, exceeding our $440-450 million guidance high end, with 26% YoY growth accelerating from Q3's 22% and 15% QoQ. Enterprise billings over $1 million ACV hit $285 million, up 35% YoY, including eight-figure wins like ZTNA for a top U.S. bank and XDR expansions atop CrowdStrike for a European energy firm. Commercial billings reached $167 million, up 18% YoY, with strong Cortex XDR add-ons for SMBs.

Regions showed balance: Americas $265 million, up 24% YoY (59% mix), via CISA mandates and hyperscaler co-sells; EMEA $110 million, up 32% YoY on NIS2 and OT needs for Siemens-like deals; APJ $77 million, up 22% YoY on Japan's My Number compliance.

AI-native Cortex drove 45% billings growth amid 300% AI-malware rise; OT/IoT added $25 million; SASE partnerships contributed 15% new ACV. Current RPO ended at $3.2 billion, up 28% YoY, future RPO up 25%, with 95%+ renewals. Headwinds like EMEA commercial delays and FX were navigated.

Our R&D investment underscores our innovation moat in a landscape of AI polymorphic malware, quantum challenges, and APTs. We spent $178 million, or 29.7% of revenue—up 320 bps YoY from 26.5% and 180 bps sequentially—versus industry 19-21%, outpacing Zscaler's 22-24% and SentinelOne's 26-27%. TTM intensity at 28.2%.

Allocations: 45% ($80 million) to AI/ML threat intelligence, shipping Nebula AI Guardian with 98.5% zero-day detection and 40% MTTR reduction; 25% ($45 million) to SASE with quantum-safe Kyber/Dilithium; 20% ($36 million) to endpoint/cloud with eBPF and Rust tooling; 10% ($17 million) to homomorphic encryption, DID, and 150 PhD hires.

Regionally tilted: North America 55% for CMMC/SEC rules; EMEA 25% for NIS2/GDPR; APAC 15% for Lazarus threats; global CoEs in Tel Aviv/Bangalore. This pressured margins to 18.2% non-GAAP but rule of 70 at 82 signals leverage; patents up 45% YoY. Guide FY24 R&D at 28-29%, trending to 26-27% FY25.

Competitive win rates hit 68%, up 450 bps QoQ and 1,000 bps YoY from 58%, above Gartner/IDC 55-60% benchmarks. EDR/XDR at 74%, displacing CrowdStrike 62% via graph neural networks and Zero-Day Challenge (82% PoC wins); SASE/ZTNA 65% vs. Zscaler/Palo Alto with PQC; CWPP 59% vs. Wiz/Orca.

Regions: North America 70% on FedRAMP/CMMC; EMEA 72% on GDPR/NHS wins; APAC 64% with Japan at 71%; LatAm 55%. $250 million FY24 AI/partner spend, AWS/Microsoft co-engineer, WinBack reclaimed 65%. Q3 guide 70-72% with HyperShield AI.

Platform adoption reached 78% of ACV, up from 62% YoY and 45% two years ago; point products <15%, down 35% YoY—industry shift per Gartner where platforms dominate 70% deals. Customers flee 45+ tools, 10,000 alerts, 40-60% TCO bloat. Our platform unifies with Quantum AI, sub-5-second latency, 3x better; Modular Fusion (92% three-module activation in 90 days, 4.2 attach, 128% NRR); AI prioritization (MITRE 100% detection); OT/IoT next.

North America 85% mix; EMEA 72%; APAC 68% rocket. Land-and-expand: 45% Q2 bookings from upsell, RPO $4.2 billion (82% platform), 50-65% TCO savings. Expect 85%+ by year-end, 81% gross margins.

For Q3 billings, we guide $272-282 million, 10-14% QoQ and 25-28% YoY, on track for FY25 $1.15-1.18 billion (24% growth). Embeds $5-8 million federal deferrals, offset by cloud upside.

Segments: Network Security (45%) $122-127 million on NGFW/SASE, ZTNA renewals 18%, SD-WAN wins; Cloud (35%) $95-99 million, CNAPP 35% YoY via AWS/Azure GenAI integrations; Endpoint/Identity (20%) $55-56 million, XDR 28% YoY.

Regions: Americas 52% ($141-147 million, 26% YoY federal); EMEA 28% ($76-79 million, 30% YoY NIS2/DORA); APAC 20% ($55-56 million, 18% YoY PDPA/APRA). DBNER 118%, 47 $1M+ ACV deals.

Macro: $212 billion market 2025, ransomware up 25%; regs like EU AI Act. R&D $45 million (22%), sales/marketing 28%, channel 42%. Risks: inflation, FX, competition. FCF 25% margins.

Now, over to Dr. Lena Novak.

Dr. Lena Novak: Thank you, Michael. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include ramping R&D to 29.7% of revenue, with heavy allocation to AI/ML for 98.5% zero-day detection in Nebula AI Guardian, quantum-safe SASE, eBPF endpoint protection, and emerging homomorphic encryption—outpacing peers to build defensible moats in XDR and beyond.

Tom Hargrove: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape—from AI-generated malware to nation-state APTs—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with 99.999% uptime SLAs and autonomous SOAR reducing MTTR by 50%.

Rachel Kim: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals—financial services at 40%, healthcare 25%, manufacturing 20%. Our sales team is executing well, expanding channel partnerships with hyperscalers and VARs to 42% of billings, driving 68% competitive win rates and 78% platform adoption.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Michael, can you elaborate on the ARR drivers and how sustainable is the 14.8% QoQ acceleration?

Michael Chen: Thanks, John. Absolutely sustainable, as evidenced by our 11th straight quarter of acceleration outpacing peers' 8-10%. Net new $68 million was 70% from expansions, DBNER 118%, and modules like GenAI seeing 3x uptake. Regional balance, hyperscaler ramps, and ThreatLynx synergies position us for 13-15% Q3 QoQ toward $2.25-2.3 billion FY24.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great results. On R&D at nearly 30%, how does that impact margins, and what's the ROI timeline?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Lisa. Short-term pressure to 18.2% non-GAAP ops, but rule of 70 at 82 shows path to leverage as revenue compounds from $2.4 billion ARR base. ROI via Nebula's 40% MTTR cuts, patent surge 45% YoY, NVIDIA/AWS partnerships—trending to 26-27% intensity FY25 while capturing $75 billion XDR market.

Operator: Next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel: Alex or Lena, thoughts on competitive dynamics? Win rates impressive—any specific bakeoff takeaways?

Dr. Lena Novak: Thanks, David. Our 68% win rate, especially 74% in EDR/XDR displacing CrowdStrike via sub-50ms graph neural nets and 82% PoC conversions on MITRE sims, stems from velocity like PQC integrations and HyperShield previews. Q3 70-72% as AI deception tech counters LockBit evolutions.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emily Rodriguez: Tom, with rising regs like NIS2, how is the threat landscape evolving, and platform shift implications?

Tom Hargrove: Emily, threats like 2,200 weekly ransomware and GenAI risks demand platforms—our 78% ACV mix unifies EDR/XDR/SASE/CNAPP/ZTNA, cutting alert fatigue and blind spots. NIS2/DORA fuel EMEA 30% YoY billings; our Frankfurt sovereignty and ITDR close DAX deals amid Okta-like breaches.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
